title: Synergies and breakeven
objectives: Answer out loud: What are breakeven synergies?
Answer out loud: Why do synergies take time?

blocks.body: Breakeven synergies: the pre-tax synergies needed to make pro forma EPS equal standalone EPS.

blocks.title: How do you calculate breakeven synergies?
blocks.teaser: Required pro forma net income = standalone EPS × pro forma shares.
blocks.body: Required pro forma net income = standalone EPS × pro forma shares. The shortfall vs. pro forma NI (excluding synergies) is the after-tax synergy needed. Divide by (1 − t) to get pre-tax.

blocks.title: Are synergies realized immediately?
blocks.body: No. They phase in over 2–3 years, and achieving them usually requires one-time integration costs (severance, systems). Year-one accretion often looks worse than steady state.

blocks.title: If breakeven synergies are small, is the deal safe?
blocks.teaser: Safer on EPS, but still not proof of value creation.
blocks.body: Safer on EPS, but still not proof of value creation. Compare the total synergies needed to justify the premium paid: the capitalized value of synergies should exceed the premium.

blocks.prompt: A deal needs only small breakeven synergies to avoid dilution. Does that prove it creates value?

options.text: Yes — EPS neutrality means it's a good deal
No — the capitalized value of synergies should exceed the premium paid
Yes, as long as the synergies are cost synergies
No — breakeven synergies are irrelevant to M&A

blocks.explanation: Breakeven synergies only test EPS. Value creation requires the capitalized synergies to exceed the premium paid.
